subject.title: [Security] Lack of rate limiting on custom channel reactions in status notifications

question: Does a current supported channel or authenticated Gateway client have a concrete path for submitting unbounded reaction events, and is the supplied evidence sufficient to treat it as a security defect?
rationale: The issue carries a protected security signal, but its cited files and proposed queue-layer repair do not match the known reaction ownership path, so maintainer-led validation is required before selecting a security boundary or disclosing implementation details.

options.title: Request concrete reproduction
options.body: Ask for the channel, exact frame or provider event, auth state, payload example, rate, logs, version, and measured memory or queue growth before choosing a fix.

options.title: Run an internal reaction audit
options.body: Audit supported channel reaction handlers and generic system-event admission for payload bounds, sender authorization, deduplication, and burst controls.

options.title: Reject the reported path
options.body: Close only after a maintainer confirms that no supported client can reach the alleged WebSocket-to-reaction path and documents the actual supported boundary.

recommendation.title: Request concrete reproduction
recommendation.body: Ask for the channel, exact frame or provider event, auth state, payload example, rate, logs, version, and measured memory or queue growth before choosing a fix.

likelyOwner.reason: They reviewed and merged the recent reaction-notification ownership work and are best positioned to validate whether the reported path matches supported behavior.
